purpose: rapidcsv is a header-only C++ CSV parser library.

functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRow: `GetRow` retrieves a row as `std::vector<T>` by row label or zero-based index, with optional conversion. If a named row isn’t found, it throws `std::out_of_range`. Example: `doc.GetRow<std::string>("2017-02-22")` in `ex003.cpp`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetRowName: Design: assign/update a row label and keep the name→row index map in sync. Use with a zero-based data row index and a name. If row-name column index < 0, it throws `out_of_range`; otherwise it grows `mData`/row width as needed and stores the name.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::RemoveColumn: Removes a column by zero-based index (or by name via overload). It maps to the data-column index, erases that entry from each row at/after the column-name row, throws `std::out_of_range` if any affected row lacks that column, then updates column names.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetColumn: `SetColumn` writes a whole column by index or name. It auto-expands rows/columns if needed, converts each value to string, and stores it in the CSV data. Use it to replace/add a column; if the column is beyond current size, missing cells/rows are created.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnNames: Returns the CSV’s column header names. Use it to inspect/check if a column exists (e.g., `find` in the returned vector). If no column-name row is configured or available, it returns an empty vector.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnName: Returns the header/name for a zero-based data column. It maps `pColumnIdx` via `GetDataColumnIndex()`, then reads the configured column-name row. If `mColumnNameIdx < 0`, it throws `std::out_of_range`; otherwise it may also throw from `at()` on invalid indices.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnCount: Returns the count of data columns, excluding any row-name/label column. It uses the first data row (or `mColumnNameIdx` if set) and subtracts `mRowNameIdx+1`; if the result is negative or no row exists, it returns 0.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter::ToStr: `ToStr()` converts a numeric `T` to CSV text for `Converter`. Use/override it via `Converter<T>::ToStr()` for custom formatting. Floats/doubles use precision 9/17; ints/chars use stream output. Docs show overriding conversion; no special cautions noted.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowCount: `GetRowCount()` returns the number of data rows, excluding any label/header rows. Use it to query how many rows are available for row-based reads. It computes `mData.size() - (columnNameIdx + 1)` and clamps negative results to `0`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Clear: `Clear()` resets a `rapidcsv::Document` to an empty state: it erases all loaded data, column names, and row names, and clears encoding flags (`mIsUtf16`, `mIsLE`, `mHasUtf8BOM`). Use it to reuse the same `Document` object for new CSV content.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Save: `Document::Save` writes the CSV data back to disk/stream. Use `Save(path)` to save to a new file and update the document’s stored path; use `Save()` to save to the original path. If `pPath` is empty, it keeps `mPath` and just writes via `WriteCsv()`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnIdx: Returns the zero-based data-column index for a named header. Use it when column labels are enabled and unique. If the name is missing or labels aren’t configured, it returns -1. Duplicate names are undefined.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetColumnName: `SetColumnName` assigns/renames the header for a zero-based data column. It requires `mColumnNameIdx >= 0` or throws `out_of_range`. It updates the name→index map, removes the old name if present, and grows the header row/table as needed.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetRow: `SetRow` writes a row into the CSV at a given zero-based row index or by row label. It auto-expands missing rows, and if the input row is wider than current columns, it resizes data rows. Values are converted to strings before storing.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowName: `GetRowName(pRowIdx)` returns the row label for a zero-based data row. Use it only when `LabelParams::pRowNameIdx >= 0` (e.g. set to 0 for first-column row headers). Otherwise it throws `out_of_range`. No direct example shown; docs mention `GetRowNames()`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumn: GetColumn reads a whole column by zero-based index or label and returns it as `vector<T>`, converting each cell via default or custom `ConvFunc<T>`. It skips label rows; out-of-range columns throw `std::out_of_range`. Example: `doc.GetColumn<float>("Close")`.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter::ToVal: `ToVal()` converts a CSV string to a numeric `T`. It’s meant to be overridden/specialized for custom parsing. Example: README `Converter<int>::ToVal()` in `ex008.cpp`; also `tests/test035.cpp`. It may throw on invalid/out-of-range input.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowIdx: Returns the zero-based data-row index for a row label. Use it only when row labels are enabled and unique; otherwise it returns -1. If the name exists, it subtracts the header/column-name offset.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Load: `Load` populates a `Document` from a CSV file path or input stream, storing parse params then reading via `ReadCsv()`. Use it to reload data with custom labels/separators/converters/line handling. Docs show file, stream/stringstream, and comment-line skipping; streams should be opened `binary`.
functions.rapidcsv::no_converter::what: `rapidcsv::no_converter::what()` is the exception message accessor. It’s used when a requested CSV value/type conversion isn’t supported. Calling `what()` returns the fixed string `"unsupported conversion datatype"`; it has no other behavior or parameters.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetCell: `GetCell` reads one CSV cell as type `T`, by zero-based indices or by row/column labels, with optional custom conversion. It uses `std::string` storage + standard conversion; `char` is the first byte. Examples show string/int/numeric reads.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::InsertColumn: `InsertColumn` inserts a column at `pColumnIdx` in the data area. Use `pColumn` to supply values; if empty, it creates a blank column sized to current data rows. `pColumnName` sets the column label. It converts `T` to strings and aligns with label/header offsets.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetCell: `SetCell` writes a value into the CSV at a given cell, using row/column index or name overloads. It auto-expands rows/columns as needed, converts `T` to string, and stores it in `mData`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::RemoveRow: Removes a data row from the CSV document by zero-based row index (or by row name in the other overload). If the index maps past `mData.size()`, it throws `std::out_of_range`. After erasing, it updates row names.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::InsertRow: Adds a row at zero-based data index. If `pRow` is empty, it inserts a blank row sized to current columns. Otherwise values are converted to strings and placed after the row-name column. If index is beyond current rows, empty rows are appended first.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter<std::basic_string<ch: `ToVal()` converts a CSV string to a numeric `T`. It’s meant to be specialized/overridden for custom parsing. It uses `stoi/stol/stoll` and range-checks small integer types; out-of-range throws. Example: `Converter<int>::ToVal` in README/ex008.cpp.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowNames: `GetRowNames()` returns the row-label strings from a `Document` when row names are enabled (`mRowNameIdx >= 0`). It skips header rows (`<= mColumnNameIdx`) and returns an empty vector otherwise. Docs mention it for checking whether a row name exists; no special caveats shown.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter<std::basic_string<ch: `Converter<std::string>::ToStr` formats a value to text for CSV output. Use it via `Converter<T>` specializations to override string conversion. It uses default formatting, with higher precision for float/double. Docs show overriding `ToVal()`/`ToStr()`; no specific caveats noted.
